top_stories.title: Claude Code leak exposes a Tamagotchi-style 'pet' and an always-on agent
top_stories.summary: A leak of Anthropic's Claude Code source code has revealed unreleased features including a Tamagotchi-style virtual pet and an always-on background agent. The leak offers a rare look at Anthropic's product roadmap and the direction of its agentic AI development. The Verge reports the findings based on the exposed code.

top_stories.title: Gradient Labs gives every bank customer an AI account manager
top_stories.summary: OpenAI has highlighted Gradient Labs, a startup using its models to give every bank customer access to a personalised AI account manager. The product aims to bring the experience of a dedicated financial adviser to retail banking at scale. The announcement was made via OpenAI's official blog.

top_stories.title: You can now use ChatGPT with Apple's CarPlay
top_stories.summary: OpenAI has integrated ChatGPT with Apple's CarPlay, allowing drivers to interact with the AI assistant hands-free while on the road. The feature expands ChatGPT's reach into automotive contexts, building on the earlier integration with Apple's Siri. The Verge reports the rollout is now live.

top_stories.title: AI benchmarks are broken. Here's what we need instead.
top_stories.summary: MIT Technology Review reports that current AI benchmarks are increasingly unreliable as a measure of real-world model performance, with many tests being saturated or gamed by developers. Researchers argue the field needs new evaluation frameworks that better reflect genuine capabilities and limitations. The piece surveys proposed alternatives and the challenges of building more meaningful assessments.

top_stories.title: I Asked ChatGPT What WIRED's Reviewers Recommend. Its Answers Were All Wrong
top_stories.summary: Wired tested ChatGPT by asking it to summarise product recommendations made by WIRED's own reviewers, and found the answers were consistently inaccurate. The experiment raises questions about the reliability of AI-generated summaries of published journalism and the risks of readers using chatbots as proxies for editorial content. The findings are relevant to ongoing debates about AI accuracy and its impact on media.

further_links.title: Meta Adaptive Ranking Model: Bending the Inference Scaling Curve to Serve LLM-Scale Models for Ads
further_links.summary: Meta's engineering blog details a new adaptive ranking model that applies LLM-scale inference to advertising, improving ad relevance while managing compute costs.

further_links.title: The gig workers who are training humanoid robots at home
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review examines how gig workers are being recruited to generate training data for humanoid robots, part of a growing trend of outsourcing embodied AI data collection.

further_links.title: Art schools are being torn apart by AI
further_links.summary: The Verge reports on deepening divisions within art schools over generative AI, as educators and students clash over whether and how AI tools should be used in creative education.

further_links.title: Accelerating the next phase of AI
further_links.summary: OpenAI's official blog outlines its vision for the next phase of AI development, touching on scaling, deployment, and societal impact.

further_links.title: The Download: AI health tools and the Pentagon's Anthropic culture war
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review's daily briefing covers the state of AI-powered health tools and reports on a cultural and political dispute within the Pentagon over its use of Anthropic's AI.

further_links.title: Open to Work: How to Get Ahead in the Age of AI
further_links.summary: Microsoft's official blog offers guidance on skills and strategies for workers navigating an AI-transformed job market.

further_links.title: Baidu's robotaxis froze in traffic, creating chaos
further_links.summary: Baidu's Apollo robotaxi fleet experienced a widespread freeze during operation in China, stranding vehicles in traffic and raising questions about autonomous vehicle reliability.

further_links.title: Shifting to AI model customization is an architectural imperative
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review argues that enterprises must move beyond off-the-shelf AI models and invest in customisation to remain competitive.

further_links.title: AI has flooded all the weather apps
further_links.summary: Wired examines how AI-generated forecasts and summaries have proliferated across weather applications, with mixed results for accuracy and user experience.

further_links.title: You can order Grubhub and Uber Eats 'conversationally' with Alexa Plus
further_links.summary: Amazon's Alexa Plus now supports conversational food ordering via Grubhub and Uber Eats, marking an expansion of agentic AI capabilities in consumer voice assistants.

ethan_mollick.title: Claude Dispatch and the Power of Interfaces
ethan_mollick.summary: Ethan Mollick explores how the interface through which you interact with AI models — including Anthropic's Claude — can dramatically shape the quality and usefulness of outputs. He argues that thoughtful interface design is underappreciated as a lever for getting more value from AI tools. The post includes practical observations on how different interaction modes affect AI performance.
